correctness.rationale: The Lindblad no-jump generator has Hamiltonian adjacency coupling J between all A and B vertices, loss kappa on every A vertex and offdiagonal projector dephasing gamma. Hilbert–Schmidt dissipation kills all nondecaying eigenmatrices for gamma>0; a diagonal B-supported survivor would create a nonzero A-B commutator. The five exact aggregate evolution equations integrate to T_gamma=(m+n)/(m kappa)+n(m-1)/(m(kappa+gamma))+(n-s)/gamma+(kappa/2+gamma)/(2mJ^2) for every m>=2,n>=1, gamma>0 and B-supported initial density of bright overlap s. For s<n the gamma=0 dark component makes the unconditional mean infinite. For bright s=n the separate two-state Hamiltonian gives T_0=2/kappa+kappa/(4mnJ^2). Strict convexity and the exact comparison polynomial F_(m,n)(x) give improvement precisely m>n and x=kappa/(J sqrt(2n(m-1)))<x_c; equality ties two distinct rates only n>=2, while n=1 equality has gamma*=0. Independent full Liouvillian numerical integration for m=3,n=2, positive rates and a complex mixed B initial state agreed with the integrated five-variable formula at <10^-14 error. This is corroboration, not proof beyond finite tests.

value.rationale: The exact question whether noise shortens *mean absorption time* of a fully bright, otherwise trapping-free initial excitation is natural in environment-assisted transport. The result distinguishes ordinary dark-state unlocking from genuine bright-state improvement, gives an explicit geometry-dependent threshold and uniquely/tied optimizers, and establishes the no-improvement regime. This is structural, not a routine one-parameter fit.
